findings.title: Installer identity check is skipped when no Integration row exists
findings.body: GitHubInstallation only compares pipeline state github_authenticated_user to metadata sender when an Integration for installation_id already exists, has no OrganizationIntegration, and is ACTIVE. If Integration.DoesNotExist, dispatch returns pipeline.next_step() immediately and never consults the OAuth login. Installation IDs are predictable integers and are supplied by the client (query string or earlier bind_state). An attacker who starts the install pipeline in their own Sentry org and supplies a victim installation_id before the installation webhook creates the Integration will pass this gate, and build_integration will attach that GitHub App installation to the attacker org with no check that the OAuth user is the installer. That is the mismatch this change claims to reject, and it is unenforced on the normal first-install path.

findings.title: Token exchange omits redirect_uri required by the authorize request
findings.body: OAuthLoginView sends redirect_uri on the GitHub authorize redirect, but the subsequent POST to the access-token URL only sends code, client_id, and client_secret. GitHub requires the same redirect_uri on the token exchange when it was included in the authorization request. The exchange will be rejected, access_token will be missing, and every install will fall through to the generic invalid-installation error. Tests stub the token endpoint and never assert the POST body, so they do not catch this.

findings.title: Sender comparison assumes metadata shape and crashes instead of failing closed
findings.body: The mismatch check indexes integration.metadata["sender"]["login"] with no existence or type guard. build_integration only stores sender when state already has it, so existing rows and installs created before the webhook (or without a sender payload) have no sender key. That raises KeyError and becomes a 500 rather than the intended error page, which both breaks legitimate reinstalls of those integrations and does not reliably fail closed. fetch_state("github_authenticated_user") can also be missing for pipelines that were already on the install step before this view was added, which either false-fails or hits the same KeyError.

findings.title: OAuth authorize URL is built by string concatenation without encoding
findings.body: The authorize redirect interpolates client_id, state, and redirect_uri into the query string with no urlencode. redirect_uri comes from absolute_uri() and is not escaped, so any reserved character (&, #, ?) splits or drops parameters. state and client_id are likewise unescaped. A crafted or future redirect_uri can change which parameters GitHub sees (for example dropping or replacing state), which weakens the CSRF check this view just added. Use urllib.parse.urlencode for the query.
